title: Clinical and physiological markers of catatonia in underlying illnesses
summary: With this study, we aim to expand our knowledge of the disorder of catatonia. Catatonia is a severe psychiatric syndrome with significant psychomotor disturbances, often in connection with another mental illness. Catatonia is highly distressing for the affected patient and can delay the return to everyday life. Treatment is directed according to the cause and is generally very successful with the correct diagnosis. Many aspects of catatonia are still unknown. In this study, we want to collect and evaluate clinical and physiological data and measurements over a period of 12 months (after the diagnosis of catatonia). In addition, we want to investigate the underlying mechanisms in the brain using magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Understanding of the study, ability and willingness to participate in the study 
- Ability to provide written informed consent as documented by signature ( Informed Consent Form) 

- Patients only: Catatonia diagnosis according to ICD-11 and presentation with a BFCRS of > 2. 
- Multiple study participation is possible for catatonia patients if patients present with a novel catatonia episode following remission of the previous one.

- Clinical/patient controls only:  matched underlying disorder, age, gender
Exclusion criteria:
None for general participation in the study, however, specific limitations apply for MRI and TMS:
- Standard exclusion criteria for MRI scanning and TMS only: 
  E.g. Medical or metal implants (retainer, pacemaker), claustrophobia, pregnancy, hearing problems/Tinnitus 

- Healthy controls only: own history of any severe mental disorder or first-degree relatives with Psychotic disorders (Bipolar, Schizophrenia).
-  Clinical/patient controls only: own history of catatonia
